  1. Write the following function. Give examples to test your function.

  • Input: a data frame

  • Output: a data frame with all the missing of numeric variables replaced by the associated means.

Hint: Similar function

library(tidyverse)
df <- read_csv('Data/titanic.csv') %>%
  select(Survived, Pclass, Sex, Age, SibSp, Fare, Embarked) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Survived, Pclass), factor))

mean_impute_df <- function(d) {
  for (i in 1:length(d)) {
    if (is.numeric(d[[i]])) {
      d[[i]][is.na(d[[i]])] <- mean(d[[i]], na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  }
  return(d)
}
colSums(is.na(df))
## Survived   Pclass      Sex      Age    SibSp     Fare Embarked 
##        0        0        0      177        0        0        2
colSums(is.na(mean_impute_df(df)))
## Survived   Pclass      Sex      Age    SibSp     Fare Embarked 
##        0        0        0        0        0        0        2
  1. Write the following function. Give examples to test your function.

  • Input: a data frame

  • Output: a data frame with all the missing of variables replaced by the associated means (for numeric variables) or modes (for non-numeric variables).

Hint: Use If-statement to combine the function in Problem 1 and the function in this example

mode_impute <- function(x) {
  if (!is.numeric(x)) {
    x <- replace_na(x, names(sort(-table(x)))[1])
  }
  return(x)
}
impute_df <- function(d) {
  d <- mean_impute_df(d)
  for (i in 1:length(d)) {
    d[[i]] <- mode_impute(d[[i]])
  }
  return(d)
}
colSums(is.na(impute_df(df)))
## Survived   Pclass      Sex      Age    SibSp     Fare Embarked 
##        0        0        0        0        0        0        0
  1. Write the following function. Give examples to test your function.

  • Input: a data frame

  • Output: Bar plots of all non-numeric variables

Hint: Similar function

bar_plot <- function(d) {
  for (i in 1:length(d)) {
    if (!is.numeric(d[[i]])) {
      print(ggplot(d, aes(x = d[[i]])) + geom_bar() + labs(x = names(d)[i]))
    }
  }
}
bar_plot(df)

  1. Write the following function. Give examples to test your function.

  • Input: a data frame

  • Output: all possible the bar plots of a non-numeric variable filled by a non-numeric variable.

Hint: Similar function

bar_plot2 <- function(d) {
  l <- length(d)
  for (i in 1:(l - 1)) {
    for (j in (i + 1):l) {
      if (!is.numeric(d[[i]]) & !is.numeric(d[[j]])) {
        print(ggplot(d, aes(x = d[[i]], fill = d[[j]])) +
                geom_bar(position = 'dodge') +
                labs(x = names(d)[i], fill = names(d)[j]))
      }
    }
  }
}
bar_plot2(df)

  1. Write the following function. Give examples to test your function.

  • Input: a data frame

  • Output:

    • all possible the bar plots of a non-numeric variable filled by a non-numeric variable.

    • all possible the density plots of a numeric variable colored by a non-numeric variable

    • all possible the scatter plots.

Hint: Combine this function, this function, and the function in Question 4. One way to combine is creating a new function, quick_plot, and call these three functions within quick_plot.

density_plot2 <- function(d) {
  for (i in 1:length(d)) {
    for (j in 1:length(d)) {
      if (is.numeric(d[[i]]) & !is.numeric(d[[j]])) {
        print(ggplot(d, aes(x = d[[i]], color = d[[j]])) + geom_density() +
                labs(x = names(d)[i], color = names(d)[j]))
      }
    }
  }
}
scatter_plot <- function(d) {
  l <- length(d)
  for (i in 1:(l - 1)) {
    for (j in (i + 1):l) {
      if (is.numeric(d[[i]]) & is.numeric(d[[j]])) {
        print(ggplot(d, aes(x = d[[i]], y = d[[j]])) + geom_point() +
                labs(x = names(d)[i], y = names(d)[j]))
      }
    }
  }
}
quick_plot <- function(d) {
  bar_plot2(d)
  density_plot2(d)
  scatter_plot(d)
}
quick_plot(df)
